info.title: Agent hub /v1 contract — single source of truth for hub<->consumer surface
info.description:
GENERATED from contract/v1.json and contract/errors.json by scripts/emit-openapi.mjs — do not edit this file; edit the contract and regenerate.

This document covers the HTTP surface only. The adapter protocol (the hub talking to a harness plugin over stdio JSON-RPC) is NOT HTTP and lives in contract/adapter-v1.json, which is machine-checked against every manifest, every request the hub sends, every event an adapter emits and every event the hub handles.

The running hub reports the exact contract it was built against at GET /v1/hub/surface (`contract.sha256`), so a client can prove which document it is talking to.

Paths, request shapes, response shapes, SSE event objects and error codes live here, and this file is checked, not merely written down: the hub reports its own surface at GET /v1/hub/surface and the hub refuses to START when the two disagree in either direction (boot self-check, server.mjs). So change this file when you change the surface — the check is what makes that instruction true instead of a hope. Adapter-facing surface lives in adapter-v1.json.

get.description: the models THIS HARNESS CAN RUN — the single authoritative source for model selection, and the only list a caller needs (do not merge it with API 1). One query: the harness's own catalog plus every core-managed provider the harness can reach during a session, so an entry means the same thing whichever harness answered and whichever way a provider got there (native config, like dsh, or injected at session start, like pi). An injected provider is named `prts-<coreProviderId>` in every harness — one spelling, no slash (pi splits a model reference on the first slash) — and `modelProviderId` accepts that spelling or the bare `<coreProviderId>`. capability-gated; known:false = harness declares no models capability (never faked as empty). Each entry keeps its real providerId. thinkingLevels is the levels for THAT model, verbatim and unconverted; a different model may offer a different list. thinkingLevelsSource says where it came from: 'declared' (stated), 'default' (the model reasons but declares none, so the set is not controllable), 'none' (the model does not reason). A model id is unique only with its providerId; (providerId, id) is the key.

get.description: the hub's harness registry. The hub manages harnesses, not just lists them: for each one it holds whether it is enabled and which extensions and skills are installed for it. A plugin present under the plugins directory is registered on first sight, carrying the extensions its manifest declares; a plugin that is gone keeps its row marked missing. Each harness row's `availableExtensions` is the catalogue THAT plugin ships (its own `extensions/` directories, and the only extensions that harness may be given); the top-level `availableExtensions` is the union of ids across installed plugins. Extensions are installed BY the hub: before a harness runs, the hub writes that harness's selected extension directories into its data dir, and the adapter places them where its harness reads them.

patch.description: Change session configuration. modelProviderId selects another core-managed provider in the same conversation; credentials/grant precedes config/set. Supply modelId or retain the currently selected model. Provider switching requires an idle turn and is serialized against turn admission and lifecycle mutations. Session id and native ref are preserved. Missing credentials/unknown provider fail before injection. Failed application retains saved selection and drops the changed adapter so next use restores saved configuration. Applied provider/model must be confirmed by the adapter. thinkingLevel sets the harness-native thinking level for this session; unconfirmed application is reported as null plus a warning, never as the requested value. A level the model does not offer is 400 validation_failed. `title` renames the session in the HARNESS as well (the hub is not the only place a name is shown): the adapter answers with the title the harness accepted, which may differ from the one asked for (dsh normalizes and sanitises), and the session reports both — `title` what was asked, `appliedTitle` what the harness holds. Requires the harness capability `rename` (501 unsupported otherwise). A title the harness did not accept is an error, never a hub-only rename that looks applied. get.description: The skills THIS session's harness actually has, read from the harness itself (pi/jouzu: their own command list; dsh: its skill catalogue RPC) — not a list of what the hub installed. It is per SESSION, not per harness, because a catalogue depends on the session's own directory: dsh resolves the project root from the session header, and the pi family also reads the project's `.pi/skills`. The difference between installed and seen is the point: the hub writes a skill's bytes into the harness's own skills directory before its process starts, and a harness may still refuse one silently (dsh drops a skill whose name is not kebab-case, whose description is missing, whose invocation keys are camelCase, or that is not a single-level `<id>/SKILL.md` bundle). Requires the harness capability `skills` (501 unsupported otherwise). A harness that does not answer in time is reported as `known:false` with a `reason` — never as an empty catalogue: an empty list is a claim ('it has no skills') and a timeout is not evidence for it. (jouzu finishes its own startup lazily: its first answer measured 9s once and 70s once, its second 24ms.)

known.description: false when this harness cannot report a catalogue at all

reason.description: why the catalogue is unknown (present only when known is false)

post.description: Start a NEW session whose conversation ends at a completed turn of this one. The source session is not changed: same log, same ref, still usable, and it does not even need a live process. Anchor = a completed turn (the only cut every harness can make exactly; harness-native anchors — pi entry ids, dsh seq numbers — never leave the adapter). Omit afterTurnId to inherit the whole conversation. Requires the harness capability `fork`; a harness that cannot fork answers 501 unsupported rather than substituting an empty conversation. The new session carries the source's harness, provider, model, preset, plan, review, thinking level, directory and scope, and is opened by its own process forking the source — so it is usable immediately and refuses (fork_failed) rather than reporting a fork it did not get.

post.description: register a provider: `{id?, label?, url, api?, token?, scope?, declarations?}`. The id is generated when absent; a duplicate id is refused (409). `api` is the wire protocol the provider speaks in the harness vocabulary (openai-completions, anthropic-messages, openai-responses, ...); the adapter that writes the harness's own provider entry is what validates it. `declarations` is keyed by model id — what that model accepts (thinking levels, window, limits) — because a provider's model list does not carry any of it. A declaration may also carry `input` — the modalities the model takes ("text", "image") — because a model that does not state them is not advertised as taking images. A declaration may also carry `name` (the display name; the harness shows it instead of the id) and `cost` ({input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite} per million tokens, optional tiers).

get.description: API 1: the core-managed providers' catalogs — what the core owns and what it can inject, independent of any harness or session. This is NOT the model-selection source: a model can only be run where a harness reaches it, so selection reads API 2 (/v1/harnesses/{id}/models), which already includes these providers. Use API 1 to manage a provider's catalog and its enabled selection, not to pick a model for a session. Core queries its registered provider endpoint with its own credential; no credential is handed to a harness for this operation. Missing/stale catalogs are fetched; cached catalogs are reused. Each model has enabled and available flags. Failures are per provider and never replace a previous catalog with an empty one.

post.description: Ask the harness to compact the session's own conversation. The hub does not compact anything itself and does not compute the numbers: it reports what the harness says (source:'harness'). Fields a harness does not report are ABSENT, never zero — pi counts the replaced span and then estimates the rebuilt context, dsh counts the replaced span only. A harness with nothing worth compacting answers compacted:false with its own words in `detail`; a compaction that failed answers compact_failed. Refused (409 session_busy) while a turn is running, because pi's compact aborts the running turn and a hub must not throw away work to run a maintenance call. Requires the harness capability `compact` (501 unsupported otherwise). The same facts also arrive on the turn stream as `session.compacting` then `session.compacted` — including for a compaction the harness performed on its own (a full context compacts mid-turn), which nobody asked for.

bearerAuth.description: the token from <DATA_DIR>/endpoint.json. Discovery (GET /v1/harnesses) needs no token; everything else answers 401 unauthorized without it.

base.description: opaque adapter base id; never enumerated

presetId.description: the preset the session was created with (opaque id); null = harness default

appliedPreset.description: the preset the harness actually applied (proof, like appliedModel)

modelProviderId.description: which managed provider feeds this session; null = do not intervene, the harness uses its own native config. Accepts the catalog spelling `prts-<id>` or the bare `<id>`; the session reports the bare id. A model named without a provider must belong to the provider that is in effect — a model from elsewhere is refused (400 validation_failed), never accepted and left to fail mid-turn.

appliedModel.description: the model the adapter actually applied; compared against modelId (T0: a silent fallback fails loudly)

appliedProviderId.description: the provider route the adapter actually applied (prts/<id> for an injected hub provider); proof the requested provider was used, not the harness's own

plan.description: the plan mode this session asked for; null = do not intervene, the harness keeps its own state

appliedPlan.description: the plan state the adapter actually applied (proof, like appliedModel); null = no plan capability, or not yet known

review.description: ask before every tool call (the review switch); null = do not intervene

appliedReview.description: the review state the adapter actually applied (proof, like appliedModel); null = no review capability, or not yet known

cwd.description: Resolved working directory, passed to adapters as PRTS_CWD. On creation, omitted/null/empty cwd allocates a persistent core-managed directory under the existing data root. This is a working-directory boundary, not OS-level confinement.

additionalDirectories.description: extra roots the harness may activate, in addition to cwd; absolute paths. Passed through to the harness — whether a harness supports them is the harness's business, and the core neither refuses nor silently drops them. [] or null = none.

appliedAdditionalDirectories.description: what the harness reported about additionalDirectories: {requested, applied, supported, reason}. The core passes the roots through and records the harness's own answer; it never assumes they became active.

disabledTools.description: the tool names the caller asked to disable; null = never asked

appliedTools.description: the disabled set the harness reported it actually has; null = not observed. A switch that could not be confirmed must not read as success.

deleted.description: true once the session has been deleted from session/list (ACP session/delete). The record is kept; delete removes it from the list, it does not wipe it.

contentPart.description: one part of a turn's content. text is plain. image carries base64 bytes — the media type is the harness-facing one (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif), data is raw base64 with NO data: prefix.

data.description: type=image: base64 bytes, no data: prefix

tool.description: confirm | select — the kind of dialog the harness raised

options.description: for a select dialog: the choices the harness offered (e.g. Allow Once / Allow Always / Reject); decision echoes one of these

reason.description: user-supplied rejection reason when the harness asked for one (codex denied.rejection; pi/jouzu Reject with Reason). null when the harness has no such concept (dsh) or the user gave none

question.description: A harness asking the user to decide something. Distinct from `approval`: an approval permits one action (allow/deny); a question asks for an answer, possibly with several options and supporting detail, and the answer is data the harness reads back

detail.description: supporting text rendered with the question (e.g. the plan under review); never an option label

intent.description: presentation hint: what kind of decision this is. `{ kind: 'plan-review', approve: '<label>' }` says detail is a plan and names the approving label. Presentation only — the answer carries the same fields either way

answers.description: the user's answer, once given: one entry per asked question

preset.description: A preset as the CLIENT sees it: an opaque id plus metadata. Content is NOT carried cross-wire (dsh-aligned; reading a composition is reconnaissance). The harness/adapter owns what a preset id means; core does not interpret it.

id.description: opaque preset id; the only thing needed to select it

name.description: display name published by the harness; falls back to id

trust.description: shipped with the deployment or locally authored (dsh: a user preset is exactly as privileged as the plugins it names)

isDefault.description: whether a session that names no preset gets this one

broken.description: why this preset cannot compose a session; absent when it can

enabled.description: false = disabled; honest grading — adapter must not report a tool disabled unless it actually blocks it

retryable.description: whether retrying the same request unchanged can succeed — straight from contract/errors.json, the same table that decides the status, so body, status and table cannot disagree. false means something must change first (the session is busy, the state needs repair, the input is invalid).

modelInvocable.description: whether the MODEL may load it; false means a human must invoke it

origin.description: 'deployment' when it came from the plugins directory this hub was given, 'hub' when the hub installed it into its own root

source.description: the git URL this hub installed it from; null when nobody installed it (a checkout or a deployment's directory)

runtime.description: {package, version, target} as the manifest declares it; null when the plugin brings its own runtime

runtimeReady.description: whether the declared runtime command exists on disk — a filesystem fact, not a claim that the harness works

prepare.description: {state: running|ready|failed, detail, startedAt, finishedAt} of the last runtime/prepare for this plugin, or null when none ran in this process

invalid.description: why the manifest cannot be honoured; null when it can

event_turn_admitted.description: the turn is accepted and the stream is open

event_message_delta.description: one delta of the streaming answer; kind says whether it is text or the model thinking out loud

event_question_requested.description: question is not approval: this wants an ANSWER, not permission

event_plan_changed.description: plan mode changed — possibly because the HARNESS changed it (a model leaving plan when its plan is approved), which is why the hub reports it instead of assuming its own last request held

event_session_stats.description: plus whatever the harness reports about this session: tokens?, cost?, context?, turns?, messages? — a field it does not report is absent

event_session_compacting.description: the harness is rewriting its own context right now, whether or not this session asked for it

event_session_compacted.description: the same facts the compact route answers with, for a compaction the harness performed on its own

event_session_renamed.description: the HARNESS named or renamed the session (dsh titles a session from its first prompt); the hub follows instead of keeping a title only it believes in
